description: #4 — `{ if (@n > 0) { @r = 1 }; else @r = 2 }`: the `;` after a BRACED consequent ends the `if`; the `else` belongs to nothing (JS rejects it too). Base rejected it; the round-3 else-lookahead must not newly accept it. Position: match.
rationale: §5.2.3: "The statement list is logic context — the same statement grammar as a function body (§7.3) … The block MAY span any number of lines." and "No statement of the block SHALL be dropped".
